commit_message: Apply the paper's V_m(T) correction in epsilon_from_record
use_policy: MIT permits reuse with attribution. The model is re-implemented from the stored definitions rather than imported, so this project does not vendor the package; the stored copies are read-only audit evidence.

stages.polar: 21 params: 11 atom-group + 9 family scales + 1 rest scale
stages.hbond: 17 params: 15 fragment scales + 1 rare scale + 1 rest scale

model_definition_extracted.epsilon_inf_model: Clausius-Mossotti with atom-group-scaled, Boltzmann-averaged atomic polarizabilities: x = 4pi/3 * N_A * alpha_scaled[A^3] * 1e-24 / V_m, eps_inf = (1+2x)/(1-x), x capped at 0.99
model_definition_extracted.orientation_model: Onsager-Kirkwood-Froehlich: a = N_A mu_eff^2 D^2 / (9 eps0 kB T V_m), b = eps_inf + a (eps_inf+2)^2, eps = (b + sqrt(b^2 + 8 eps_inf^2))/4
model_definition_extracted.effective_dipole: mu_eff = b*mu_remainder + sum_k c_k * mu_k, Boltzmann mean square; group dipoles built from charges x positions + atomic dipoles
model_definition_extracted.molar_volume: Bouteloup & Mathieu 2019 group contributions (smi2DC), at 298.15 K, with a FIXED alpha_V = 1e-3 K^-1 for temperature correction
model_definition_extracted.conformer_protocol: RDKit ETKDGv3, GFN2-xTB/ALPB(diethyl ether), qRRHO weights

reference_predictions.note: author's own stored values for 16 liquids; used as the acceptance test of any re-implementation

reproducibility_caveats_from_author: conformer ensembles depend slightly on RDKit version and platform
predictions can deviate from the paper by a few per cent for small rings and diols
xtb 6.7.1 was used to fit; a different xtb changes conformers
what_this_repo_cannot_reproduce: The 1393-liquid training set is not shipped: only 16 reference ensembles are included. So the FIT cannot be reproduced, only the MODEL FORMULA can be evaluated on ensembles we generate ourselves. A like-for-like comparison must therefore be run on a common molecule set with a common conformer protocol, and the author's published CV numbers must not be quoted against our MAE.
